summary: The starter prompt gives a clear, implementable goal (Node.js + Mongoose multi-currency ledger with DocumentDB transactions, idempotency keys, and aggregation-based balance queries). Several implementation details (driver versions, exact model fields, index DDL, seed scripts, README, tests, repo conventions) are not specified and will be chosen by the builder or filled in by the installed skills; none are blocking the start of the build.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js multi-currency ledger using Mongoose and DocumentDB transactions... Use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate postings. Expose endpoints for posting transactions and querying balances in any base currency using aggregation."
rubric.note: Business goal and demonstration (transactions, exchange-rate references, idempotency, aggregation-based conversions) are explicitly stated.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Single-agent code sample (no multi-agent orchestration); the coding agent will produce a single Node.js app and scripts.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't name an agent framework or multi-agent workflow; this doesn't stop the app build.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Node.js and Mongoose"; skill.md: "Node.js 24 with npm and npx is available."
rubric.note: Runtime (Node.js) and availability of Node 24 are present in the run-environment skill.md.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a recent stable Mongoose compatible with Node 24 (e.g., mongoose 7.x) and the matching mongodb driver that ships with it.
rubric.note: No explicit Mongoose or MongoDB driver version/range; documentdb-driver skill gives best-practice patterns but not a pinned version.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt: 'DocumentDB'; skill.md: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol...) is reachable... use database named `sample_fintech_07`."
rubric.note: Run environment explicitly supplies the live cluster and DB name to use.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Connection string read at runtime from environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI; do not write actual secret into files or logs.
rubric.note: skill.md directs using DOCUMENTDB_URI env var and forbids embedding secrets into repository artifacts.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Store transactions with a currency field and a reference to an exchange rate document."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement Mongoose models per the reference requirements: Transaction { amount:Number, currency:String, accountId:String, exchangeRate:ObjectId ref, timestamp:Date, idempotencyKey:String } and ExchangeRate { baseCurrency:String, quoteCurrency:String, rate:Number, timestamp:Date }. Collections named transactions and exchange_rates.
rubric.note: Prompt requires transactions and exchange-rate references but doesn't enumerate every field or collection name; documentdb-data-modeling can guide normalization/embedding choices.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create a small idempotent seed script that inserts a handful of accounts, a few exchange-rate documents (EUR/USD, GBP/USD, etc.) and a couple sample transactions; seed script is idempotent (upsert by natural key or checks).
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't ask for or describe sample data or seeding; reference requirements expect a seed script but it's not provided.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "querying balances in any base currency using aggregation" and earlier references to exchange-rate references and idempotency keys.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement aggregation pipeline with $lookup to join exchange_rates and convert amounts; create a unique DB-level index on idempotencyKey (unique), and create indexes on accountId and on exchange rate lookup keys (baseCurrency+quoteCurrency, timestamp) to support efficient lookups.
rubric.note: Prompt specifies aggregation-based conversion but does not specify DB index DDL. documentdb-indexing skill provides guidance on index shapes and tradeoffs; ensure unique index on idempotencyKey as required by reference.
No embeddings, LLMs, or other AI pieces are requested for this ledger sample.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Expose endpoints for posting transactions and querying balances in any base currency using aggregation."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement an Express.js HTTP API with POST /transactions (payload: accountId, amount, currency, exchangeRateId, idempotencyKey) and GET /balances?baseCurrency=USD that returns per-account balances converted into baseCurrency.
rubric.note: Prompt requires endpoints but doesn't name exact route paths or response formats; the reference suggests POST /transactions and GET /balances?baseCurrency.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: "This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable... Use the database named `sample_fintech_07`... Do not provision another cluster unless allowed."
rubric.note: No infra provisioning required or expected for the sample; the run-environment provides the cluster to use.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Provide npm scripts and README commands: npm install, npm run seed, npm start, and basic curl examples for POST /transactions and GET /balances. Tests may be simple integration tests that run against the live cluster; if offline unit tests are required, mocks would be included.
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't ask for exact run/test commands or test coverage; reference expects README and runnable scripts.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Accept when endpoints exist and are demonstrated: posting transactions with idempotency prevents duplicates (DB-level uniqueness enforced), transactions and balance updates are performed within a Mongoose transaction, and GET /balances returns correct converted sums per account.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria in the prompt; the builder will rely on expected functional checks.

rubric.skill_that_covers: skill.md (partial guidance: do not write secrets into files)
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Keep cost low (do not provision new clusters), avoid storing secrets in repo, do not include production-grade HA or CMK changes — sample is for demonstration only.
rubric.note: No explicit cost/scale constraints or compliance instructions; skill.md gives one constraint about secrets.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Follow common Node sample layout (src/, routes/, models/, scripts/seed.js), include .env.example with placeholders, README with prerequisites/setup/run/teardown, and use the term "Azure DocumentDB" in docs.
rubric.note: Starter prompt does not specify repo layout or documentation style; reference requirements call for .env.example and README content.

questions_for_author: Should the sample maintain a separate per-account balance/ledger document (updated inside the transaction), or should balances be computed entirely from transactions at read-time? The reference requirements expect updates to a related balance/ledger document inside the DB transaction — please confirm.
Which Mongoose (and mongodb driver) version should be targeted/pinned? If none, I will pick a recent stable Mongoose compatible with Node 24 (e.g., mongoose 7.x).
Do you want explicit route names and response schemas (e.g., POST /transactions and GET /balances?baseCurrency=USD), or should the implementer choose reasonable defaults and document them in README?
requirements_at_risk: Define an ExchangeRate Mongoose model that includes baseCurrency, quoteCurrency, numeric rate, and timestamp fields — prompt implied exchange-rate documents but did not specify exact fields; builder may omit some fields unless assumed.

Create a unique index on the idempotencyKey field (DB-level uniqueness) to enforce idempotency for transaction postings — prompt asks for idempotency keys but doesn't explicitly require a DB unique index; without explicit instruction this may be missed unless the builder follows the reference.

The POST /transactions handler must rely on DB-level unique constraint when enforcing idempotency — prompt mentions idempotency but not the DB-unique-index + error-handling pattern; could be overlooked.

When posting a transaction, perform the create and balance update inside a single DocumentDB transaction (Mongoose sessions) — prompt asks for DocumentDB transactions but does not explicitly say to also update a separate balance document atomically; the reference requires it.
A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — prompt doesn't ask for seeding or idempotent seed script.
.env.example lists every setting with placeholder values — prompt/skill.md indicate env usage (DOCUMENTDB_URI) but do not require a complete .env.example artifact.

One database client is created and reused across requests — not explicitly requested in the prompt; although documentdb-driver skill recommends singleton MongoClient, the sample could still create clients per request if the implementer doesn't follow that best practice.

Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt (or equivalent for Node) — prompt doesn't require pinned deps or a lockfile; for Node the equivalent is package-lock.json or pinned package.json; this may not be included unless specified.
A seed/script and README that cover setup, run, and clean-up — prompt doesn't request a README, scripts or cleanup instructions, but gallery standards expect them.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — prompt expects verification against live cluster (skill.md), so offline unit tests that mock the DB may be missing.
Infrastructure-as-code for the cluster is provided — prompt/skill.md explicitly say a cluster already exists; the sample will likely not include ARM/Bicep/Terraform code.

The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name — prompt uses 'DocumentDB' but doesn't mandate README wording; this might be missed in documentation unless enforced.

Vector index related requirements (dimensions, parameters, README guidance) — the run-environment mentions a vector-capable cluster but the ledger sample doesn't need vector indexes; those generic gallery requirements won't be satisfied by this sample unless added intentionally.
Search-related requirements (e.g., /search error handling, similarity scores) — not relevant to this ledger sample and so will probably be absent.
